subject: polish
summary: Polish is the cleanest of this group: questions read well, every reading card attaches the correct text with no stray questions, and the written-production rubrics (cards 3 and 9) are laid out as tidy band lists that work on a phone. The recurring fault is a boilerplate note ('The examination prints this question in Polish and it is answered in POLISH. The scheme awards half marks for an answer given in the wrong language.') pasted inside the first answer box of almost every card, often longer than the answer itself and sometimes sitting above it. A few schemes are still raw: card 1 is one slash-joined string treated as a single 3-mark tick, card 6 is a wall of quoted sample sentences, and card 2's multiple-choice options are run into a paragraph. Card 3 asks the student to describe a photo that is not shown on the card, only inside the attachment. All listening audio failed to load in the capture.

issues.title: Language-rule boilerplate inside the answer box on nearly every card
issues.detail: The note 'The examination prints this question in English and it is answered in English or in Irish, not in Polish. The scheme awards half marks for an answer given in the wrong language.' (or the Polish-language variant with 'POLISH' in capitals) sits inside the first scheme point. On card 8 the answer is the single word 'four' with four lines of note under it; on cards 5, 10 and 11 the note comes ABOVE the first answer, so the first answer looks like part of the note and the other answers look like different kinds of item. Cards 5, 10, 11 add author wording ('Under the scheme's heading "Refleksje typu:": examples, not a checklist'); card 2 adds 'The scheme ticks one box and prices the whole question "(2 m)"'.
issues.suggested_fix: Take the note out of the answer boxes. Show one short line per card below the scheme ('Answer in English or Irish; half marks if answered in Polish') and label sample answers with a plain heading such as 'Example points the scheme accepts'.

issues.title: Card 6: scheme is a wall of quoted sample text
issues.detail: The 30-mark commentary card puts the language note, an explanation of the scheme's wording and four long quoted sample sentences into one grey paragraph of about 20 lines on the phone, before the four criteria. The criteria themselves (30/30/30/10 %) with 0-9 and 0-3 buttons are fine, but nothing explains what a 3 versus a 7 looks like.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the four sample ideas as a short bulleted 'ideas the scheme suggests' list, and put the four criteria first with their mark ranges.

issues.title: Card 1: slash-joined answer as one all-or-nothing tick
issues.detail: 'noisy place / parties / difficult to focus on studies / several people in one room' is a single 3-mark checkbox. It is unclear whether one reason earns 3 marks or all four are needed.
issues.suggested_fix: List the four accepted reasons as separate lines under a heading that states the rule ('Any one of these — 3 marks', if that is what the scheme says).

issues.title: Multiple-choice and table questions flattened into a sentence
issues.detail: Card 2 runs the four statements together: '...Choose one statement only. (i) Second-hand shops first appeared... (ii) There are more vintage shops... (iii)... (iv)...', and keeps 'Put a tick (✓) in the appropriate box'. Card 12 says 'Fill in the table below' and then runs the three row questions into one line with no table. Card 4 shows the gap as a long underscore run that wraps awkwardly on the phone.
issues.suggested_fix: Render card 2 as four option buttons and highlight (iv) on reveal; render card 12 as three labelled lines matching the three scheme groups; use a short fixed-width gap on card 4.

issues.title: Card 3: photo to be described is not on the card
issues.detail: The task is 'Opisz zamieszczone obok zdjęcie' (describe the photo alongside) but the card shows only text; the photo is only visible after opening the 'Read Zadanie 4' attachment, whose button does not say it contains a picture. The stem 'Wykonaj po polsku zadanie (a) lub (b), lub (c)' and the scheme lines 'Zadanie 4: (a) lub (b), lub (c) ... Zadanie 5: ...' refer to options and a question the card does not cover.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the photo inline under the question (cropped from the page) and drop the either/or stem and the Zadanie 5 line.

issues.title: Writing cards: sibling options and marker-only instructions
issues.detail: Card 9's attached page shows options (a) blog, (b) letter and (c) diary together although the card is option (b). Its scheme opens with nine lines addressed to examiners ('Candidates are required to attempt Question 3(a) or 3(b)... Mark irrelevant material on the right-hand margin'). The Expression buttons are greyed out until a content mark is chosen, which is explained only by one small line.
issues.suggested_fix: Crop the attachment to option (b) or drop it, since the full task is already typed on the card. Keep only the rules a student needs (content first; no expression marks if content is 0).

issues.title: Stem labels run into the instruction, and audio not loading
issues.detail: Listening stems join a Polish section title to the English instruction and end with an orphan item label: 'Rozmowa studentów You will hear...', 'Wiadomości You will hear three news items... Answer in English. Item 1', '...Answer in English. Item 4'. All four listening cards show 'The embedded recording could not be loaded' in the capture.
issues.suggested_fix: Put the section title and 'Item N' on their own label line; verify the audio in the live app.

good_examples.why: Clear question, right text attached, 'Any 2 of these — 2 marks each' with four short readable answers.
Rubric bands are short bullet lists with clear headings and score buttons; reads well on a phone.
Scheme grouped by the three parts of the question, each labelled, with a 'One of these' group.
